content: Autoclave tape is a specialized adhesive tape designed for use in autoclaving processes to verify whether the appropriate temperature has been achieved to ensure the complete eradication of all living microorganisms. This temperature is typically 121 degrees Celsius. Small strips of this tape are applied to items prior to their placement in the autoclave. The tape is engineered to be slightly more adhesive than standard masking tape, enabling it to adhere effectively under the high-temperature and high-humidity conditions present within the autoclave. The tape is usually marked with diagonal patterns containing a heat-sensitive ink. This ink undergoes a color change, typically from beige to black, when exposed to the required temperature. The composition of the ink includes 7% ethyl acetate and 49% ink solids. It is important to note that the specified temperature of 121 degrees Celsius must generally be maintained for a duration of 15 minutes to ensure effective sterilization.
